title: Session 1: The three books

series.title: What does the Quran say about the Bible?

opening_question: The Quran names three books that came before it: the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel. What does the Bible itself say about the law Moses wrote, the psalms of David and the gospel of Jesus?

steps.question: The Quran says the Torah and the Gospel were sent down before it. What did Moses do with the words of the law, and where was the book put?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: he hath sent down unto thee the book of the Koran with truth, confirming that which was revealed before it; for he had formerly sent down the law, and the gospel a direction unto men; and he had also sent down the distinction between good and evil. Verily those who believe not the signs of GOD shall suffer a grievous punishment; for GOD is mighty, able to revenge.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: He hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture with truth, confirming that which was (revealed) before it, even as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel aforetime, for a guidance to mankind; and hath revealed the Criterion (of right and wrong). Lo! those who disbelieve the revelations of Allah, theirs will be a heavy doom. Allah is Mighty, Able to Requite (the wrong).

facts.text: The Hebrew word torah means "a precept or statute"; the King James Version translates it "law".
Sale (1734) calls the Torah "the law"; Pickthall (1930) keeps its name, "the Torah". Deuteronomy says Moses wrote it "in a book" and it was kept beside the ark.

steps.question: The Quran says the Psalms were given to David. What does David say about the words he spoke, and what does Psalm 1 say about the law?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: Verily we have revealed our will unto thee, as we have revealed it unto Noah and the prophets who succeeded him; and as we revealed it unto Abraham, and Ismael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and unto Jesus, and Job, and Jonas, and Aaron, and Solomon; and we have given thee the Koran, as we gave the psalms unto David:

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Lo! We inspire thee as We inspired Noah and the prophets after him, as We inspired Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and as We imparted unto David the Psalms;

facts.text: "Psalmist" in 2 Samuel 23:1 is zamir: "a song to be accompanied with instrumental music".
David says "his word was in my tongue": the Spirit of the LORD spoke by him.

steps.question: The Quran says the Torah has "guidance and a light". What does the Bible call God's word and his law?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: We have surely sent down the law, containing direction, and light: thereby did the prophets, who professed the true religion, judge those who judaized; and the doctors and priests also judged by the book of GOD, which had been committed to their custody; and they were witnesses thereof. Therefore fear not men, but fear me; neither sell my signs for a small price. And whoso judgeth not according to what GOD hath revealed, they are infidels.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Lo! We did reveal the Torah, wherein is guidance and a light, by which the prophets who surrendered (unto Allah) judged the Jews, and the rabbis and the priests (judged) by such of Allah's Scripture as they were bidden to observe, and thereunto were they witnesses. So fear not mankind, but fear Me. And barter not My revelations for a little gain. Whoso judgeth not by that which Allah hath revealed: such are disbelievers.

facts.text: Psalm 119:105 uses ner, "a lamp", and or, light: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet".
Sale's Quran says the law holds "direction, and light"; Proverbs 6:23 says "the law is light".

steps.question: The Quran says Jesus was given the Gospel, "wherein is guidance and a light". How does Mark begin, and what did Jesus preach?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: We also caused Jesus the son of Mary to follow the footsteps of the prophets, confirming the law which was sent down before him; and we gave him the gospel, containing direction and light; confirming also the law which was given before it, and a direction and admonition unto those who fear God:

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: And We caused Jesus, son of Mary, to follow in their footsteps, confirming that which was (revealed) before him, and We bestowed on him the Gospel wherein is guidance and a light, confirming that which was (revealed) before it in the Torah - a guidance and an admonition unto those who ward off (evil).

facts.text: Gospel is euangelion: "a good message". Mark uses it for the message about Jesus, "the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God", and for what Jesus preached, "the gospel of the kingdom of God".

In the Quran the Gospel (Injil) is a book given to Jesus. In the New Testament "the gospel" is the good news Jesus preached and the good news about him; the four accounts of his life were later called the Gospels.

steps.question: After he rose, Jesus named the parts of Scripture that speak of him. Which three does he name, and what did he open?

facts.text: The Quran names the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel. Jesus names "the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms": the Hebrew Scriptures in three parts.
Psalm is psalmos: "a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode"; it can mean "the book of the Psalms".

remember.text: Moses wrote the law, and it was put "in the side of the ark".
"Thy word is a lamp unto my feet"
"The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God"
Jesus named "the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms" as written of him.

outside_sources.name: George Sale (1734)
outside_sources.about: The first English translation made directly from the Arabic. Sale was a Christian scholar. He did not number the verses; the numbers here are the standard ones.

outside_sources.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
outside_sources.about: The first English translation by an English Muslim, read by scholars in Cairo before it was printed. Public domain in the US (published 1930) and wherever the term is life plus 70 years (Pickthall died in 1936).
outside_sources.source: The 1930 London printing (George Allen & Unwin), checked word for word; text from Tanzil.net with its slips corrected
